correctness.rationale: Each rank-(n-a) partial injection has exactly a! full permutation extensions, hence μ_a is uniform Π restricted outside an independent uniform a-deletion set. In composing independent factors, pull deletion D_i backwards through independent prefix permutations P_{i-1}, obtaining independent uniform A_i that are independent of final uniform P_k; the product equals P_k restricted outside their union. Inclusion-exclusion gives p_s and individual-map probability p_s s!/n!. Rank conditioned product is uniform; μ_a span a commutative convolution subalgebra with normalized uniform permutation μ_0 as identity, not δ_id. For fixed a, surviving-rank chain is a deletion hypergeometric process; (r)_j are an eigenbasis with λ_j=C(n-j,a)/C(n,a); factorial moments give fixed-a Poisson and Gumbel coupon limits, with a=1 Stirling/harmonic laws classical. Checked rank fibers exactly at n≤4 for mixed profiles and hundreds of eigenfunction cases; universal coupling proof is separate.

originality.rationale: Ganyushkin–Mazorchuk 2006 §§6–7 **already prove** products of independent uniformly sampled elements of the whole IS_n have law constant on each rank and derive a rank transition matrix/eigenvectors (Lemma 8, Theorem 11); these substantial prior parts are fully credited, not claimed new. The current theorem instead fixes arbitrary rank strata μ_{a_i}, identifies the full semigroup-valued product with a random permutation restricted by independent fixed-cardinality deletion sets, gives explicit multivariate convolution constants for all deletion profiles and a fixed-batch coupon hitting-time law. The prior unconditional uniform-whole-monoid product law neither states nor directly determines the conditional multirank convolution coefficients, and its transition matrix corresponds to a mixture of deletion sizes. Best-of-knowledge PASS qualified by possible older conditioning arguments.
